message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter the trade offer from p3.

I'm tallying my holdings to evaluate the offer. I have cash and several properties, but I need to verify whether I own all three pink properties.

The offer swaps Connecticut Avenue for Illinois Avenue and Short Line. I have two of three pink properties. I am now checking p2's cash and jail status.

p2 has a dark blue monopoly with one house on each property. They also own two railroads and are missing Illinois Avenue.

p3 has cash and several light blue properties including Oriental, Vermont, and Baltic.

I am the only player who can complete the light blue monopoly. p3 already holds Oriental and Vermont, and I hold Connecticut. p4 is the richest opponent with cash of $1075. They own Mediterranean, New York, Ventnor, and North Carolina.

I should reject this trade. Giving up Connecticut Avenue would let p3 complete their light blue monopoly. I must keep it as a blocker. I also need to hold St. James Place and Pennsylvania Avenue. I will not fund p2's dark blue houses.

The trade would give me Illinois Avenue, which blocks p2 from completing their red monopoly. I would also gain a second railroad, raising my rent from $25 to $50. Still, handing over Connecticut Avenue is too large a gift for p3 to build houses on the light blues.

The light blue monopoly would cost p3 roughly $320 to build, and three houses would generate heavy rent. Illinois Avenue is a singleton red worth only about $240. Trading it to p2 later would be catastrophic because p2 already owns two railroads and dark blues, giving them the cash to complete another full monopoly.

I am weighing a counter-offer. I could request Tennessee Avenue from p3 to complete the orange monopoly, though I would still need New York Avenue from p4. I have no interest in acquiring Park Place or Boardwalk from p2.

Baltic Avenue is useless to me because p4 already owns Mediterranean. I should keep my $476 cash for Virginia and house repairs. A light blue monopoly would be better than waiting for Virginia, but I will not trade Connecticut Avenue unless I receive a comparable monopoly in return.

I considered counter-offers that would extract value without giving p3 the light blue monopoly, but none are viable. A firm reject is the correct play. I will not signal that I am willing to sell Connecticut Avenue.

I will reject the offer. I will not mention pinks or Virginia in my reply.
